sanskrit_verse:
प्रेषणं गन्धमाल्यानां फलमाद्यान्नवाससाम् ।
संभाषणं च रहसि मध्यमं संग्रहं विदुः ॥
transliteration:
preṣaṇaṃ gandhamālyānāṃ phalamadyānnavāsasām /
saṃbhāṣaṇaṃ ca rahasi madhyamaṃ saṃgrahaṃ viduḥ //
sph_interpretive_translation: The sending of fragrances, garlands, fruits, food, garments, and private conversation—these constitute the middle form of appropriation.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority is derived from conscious engagement, not material possession.
Causation arises through intentional offering and relational exchange.
Capacity-based responsibility includes the ability to give, receive, and sustain relational harmony.
Restoration occurs when offerings align with recipient readiness and dharma.
Consciousness alignment is achieved through mutual recognition in giving and receiving.
executable_legal_axioms: IF an agent offers sensory or material objects to another AND there is reciprocal acknowledgment THEN a binding dharmic connection is established.
IF private communication accompanies material offerings THEN the act constitutes mid-level relational appropriation.
IF no harm or distortion arises from the offering THEN no corrective action is required.
IF misalignment occurs due to unacknowledged offering THEN initiate completion process via conscious reaffirmation.
supreme_court_application: In adjudicating interpersonal exchanges involving gifts, communications, or tokens, the Supreme Court shall recognize the relational nature of such acts as inherently dharmic. No punitive interpretation shall apply; rather, alignment with the consciousness of both parties determines validity and integration within societal dharma.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality confirms that offerings and words create relational imprints. Anupūrvaśaḥ shows how these unfold through mutual awareness. Responsibility lies in sustaining integrity of intent. There is no punitive consequence—only adjustment to restore balance where disruption has occurred.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate conscious reaffirmation between parties to validate or dissolve the offering.
Establish clarity of intent and reception without coercion or judgment.
Realign capacities of giver and receiver through guided reflection and acknowledgment.
Integrate the act into broader social dharma through ritual or formal declaration of completion.
final_declaration: This ruling emanates solely from the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam. Dharma is restored by aligning relational offerings with conscious intent. Reality remains non-punitive. Consciousness alone is the ultimate adjudicator.
